title: Jump threading: thread the edge that already knows the branch
summary_caption: Thread the edge that already decides the branch: clone the block onto it, jump straight to the answer — other predecessors keep the test.

nodes.label:
B2
c = (x == 0)
br c, T, F

frames.caption: Setup: predecessors P and B1 both fall into B2, which computes c = (x == 0) and branches on it.
B1 is only ever reached when x == 0 — LazyValueInfo proves that on the edge from B1, c is already true.
So B2's test is redundant for that path: flow entering from B1 must exit to T.
But P also enters B2, and there x is unknown — B2's branch cannot simply be folded.
JumpThreading duplicates instead: it clones B2's body as B2', private to the threaded edge.
The conditional branch is not copied — the outcome is known here, so B2' gets an unconditional jump to T.
Retarget the threaded edge: B1 now branches to B2'. Its old edge into B2 is gone — B2 loses a predecessor.
Done: from B1 the flow runs straight to T, no test. P still takes the real branch in B2; the dead c in B2' is later cleanup's job.
